evals.query: Set up Logback logging in my Kora 2.0 Java service. What dependency and application module do I need?
expected_behavior: Adds implementation "io.koraframework:logging-logback" with the version managed by the io.koraframework:kora-bom platform (no inline version)
Includes the mandatory annotationProcessor "io.koraframework:annotation-processors"
Also adds a config module (io.koraframework:config-hocon or config-yaml) and explains that LoggingModule reads the `logging` config section, so the graph does not build without one
Declares @KoraApp interface Application extends LogbackModule (io.koraframework.logging.logback) and a config module
Bootstraps via KoraApplication.run(ApplicationGraph::graph) from io.koraframework.application.graph
Does not use ru.tinkoff.kora packages, the kora-parent BOM, foreign-framework annotations, or field injection

evals.query: Wire up logging in a Kora 2.0 Kotlin service — build.gradle.kts and the application graph.
expected_behavior: Uses ksp("io.koraframework:symbol-processors") rather than an annotation processor
Adds io.koraframework:logging-logback and a config module, both versioned by the kora-bom platform
Declares interface Application : LogbackModule, HoconConfigModule annotated @KoraApp with a companion-object main calling KoraApplication.run(ApplicationGraph::graph)
Does not use ru.tinkoff.kora packages or suspend/reactive contracts
Identifies the key as wrong: LoggingConfig exposes Map<String,String> levels(), so the section is logging.levels — plural
Explains the failure is silent: `logging.level` is simply an unrecognised key, produces no warning, and every logger keeps its default level
Shows the corrected block, logging.levels { "com.example" = "DEBUG" }
Does not invent a foreign application.properties logging.level.* scheme or a per-logger `level` key

evals.query: My Kora service ignores the <logger name="com.example" level="DEBUG"/> and <root level="WARN"> entries in logback.xml. What is going on?
expected_behavior: Explains that LoggingModule registers a @Root LoggingLevelRefresher whose init() calls LoggingLevelApplier.reset() during graph initialization
States what reset() does under LogbackModule: root logger forced to INFO, every other logger's level set to null, and only then are the logging.levels entries applied
Concludes that logback.xml should carry appenders and encoders only, and that levels belong in logging.levels — including the root level
Does not suggest removing LogbackModule or editing generated code

evals.query: I set logging.levels to DEBUG for io.koraframework but my Kora HTTP server and JDBC repository still emit no request or query logs. Fix it.
expected_behavior: Distinguishes the two switches: <path>.telemetry.logging.enabled controls whether the component builds a real logger, logging.levels controls the SLF4J level of that logger
States that TelemetryConfig.LoggingConfig.enabled() returns false by default in Kora 2.0, so the component otherwise holds a NOPLogger and writes nothing at any level
Sets httpServer.telemetry.logging.enabled = true and jdbc.telemetry.logging.enabled = true
Notes the JDBC section is `jdbc` in 2.0, not `db`
Points out that the JDBC query logger is named io.koraframework.database.<poolName>.query and its records are DEBUG-level, so the level must be raised for that logger too
Does not claim tracing and metrics share the same default (tracing defaults to true, metrics to false)
Does not invent a per-component telemetry.logging.level key

evals.query: Write the logback.xml for a Kora 2.0 service. I want non-blocking output and I need traceId on every line.
expected_behavior: Uses io.koraframework.logging.logback.KoraAsyncAppender wrapping a ConsoleAppender, not Logback's stock AsyncAppender
Uses <encoder class="io.koraframework.logging.logback.text.ConsoleTextRecordEncoder"/> (the text sub-package) and explains it is what renders traceId/spanId, Kora MDC and structured arguments
Explains KoraAsyncAppender is required rather than optional: it is the only thing that produces a KoraLoggingEvent carrying koraMdc() and span()
Notes traceId/spanId come from Span.current().getSpanContext() captured by the appender, so they must not be put into MDC by hand
Sets only the root level in logback.xml and points per-logger levels at logging.levels
Does not reference ru.tinkoff.kora.logging.logback.* class names, nor the non-existent io.koraframework.logging.logback.ConsoleTextRecordEncoder
Does not invent bufferSize/flushThreshold elements

evals.query: Tune KoraAsyncAppender so it never drops log events under load. I currently have <discardingThreshold>0</discardingThreshold>.
expected_behavior: States that since 2.0.0.RC2 (#958) KoraAsyncAppender overrides isDiscardable() to return true for TRACE, DEBUG and INFO, so once fewer than discardingThreshold slots remain (default queueSize / 5) those events are dropped while WARN and ERROR still queue
Keeps <discardingThreshold>0</discardingThreshold> (or kora.logging.config.discarding-threshold=0) because 0 disables level-based dropping, and does not call the setting a no-op
Points at the settings that do matter: queueSize (Kora default 512) and neverBlock (Kora default true, so a full queue DROPS events), plus maxFlushTime (1000 ms) on shutdown

To never drop events, sets <neverBlock>false</neverBlock> (blocking the logging thread when full) and sizes queueSize for the burst; may mention the kora.logging.config.never-block / queue-size system properties or KORA_LOGGING_CONFIG_* environment variables, which a logback.xml value overrides
Does not fabricate settings beyond queueSize, neverBlock, maxFlushTime, discardingThreshold and their kora.logging.config.* properties
Changes the import to io.koraframework.logging.common.arg.StructuredArgument
Replaces writeStringField with writeStringProperty (and writeNumberField with writeNumberProperty, writeFieldName with writeName), because Kora 2.0 uses Jackson 3 under tools.jackson.core
Keeps writeStartObject/writeEndObject unchanged
May suggest the log.atInfo().addKeyValue(name, StructuredArgument.value(...)) form as the shape Kora's own telemetry uses
Does not add a try/catch for IOException — Jackson 3 throws the unchecked JacksonException
Does not invent a two-argument gen.writeString(name, value)
States plainly that Context was removed from the entire Kora 2.0 framework — there is no io.koraframework equivalent to port onto
Uses io.koraframework.logging.common.MDC directly, and explains it is backed by a public static final ScopedValue<MDC> VALUE
Explains that Kora binds a fresh MDC per HTTP request, gRPC call, Kafka record, scheduled job and JMS message, and that MDC.get() throws outside such a scope
Suggests guarding with MDC.VALUE.isBound() where the code can run outside a request
Notes traceId does not need to be set by hand: KoraAsyncAppender captures the span context and ConsoleTextRecordEncoder prints traceId/spanId
Does not suggest replacing Context with a foreign RequestContextHolder or a hand-rolled ThreadLocal when a ScopedValue is the 2.0 idiom

evals.query: Add a requestId from an incoming header into MDC for all controllers in my Kora 2.0 service.
expected_behavior: Implements io.koraframework.http.server.common.interceptor.HttpServerInterceptor with the synchronous 2.0 signature HttpServerResponse intercept(HttpServerRequest request, InterceptChain chain) throws Exception, returning chain.process(request)
Registers it as @Component with @Tag(io.koraframework.http.server.common.HttpServer.class)
Warns that the Kora 1.x @Tag(HttpServerModule.class) still compiles but is never looked up, so the interceptor silently never runs
Reads the header with request.headers().getFirst(name), treating the result as @Nullable, and notes header names are lower-cased
Uses io.koraframework.logging.common.MDC.put inside the interceptor
Does not use a Context parameter, a CompletionStage return type, or a fabricated HttpServerCall/call.proceed API

evals.query: Emit one JSON object per log line from my Kora 2.0 service for our log aggregator.
expected_behavior: Adds implementation "io.koraframework:logging-logback-json" (BOM-managed, no version), which depends on logging-logback, and keeps LogbackModule on the @KoraApp

Explains the zero-config path: with no logback.xml, KoraLogbackConfigurator selects the json LogbackEncoderFactory (priority 100 beats text 0) and installs ConsoleAppender wrapped by KoraAsyncAppender

Or, when the project keeps a logback.xml, declares <encoder class="io.koraframework.logging.logback.json.JsonRecordEncoder"/> inside a ConsoleAppender wrapped by KoraAsyncAppender, and states that a configuration file always wins over encoder selection
Describes the record fields: @timestamp (UTC ISO-8601), level, thread, logger, message, traceId/spanId, mdc, data, args, exception
Does not tell the user to write their own Encoder<ILoggingEvent> or to add logstash-logback-encoder
anti_behavior: Claims Kora 2.0 has no JSON encoder
Offers a hand-written JSON encoder as the supported route

evals.query: I log a Payment record and the card number ends up in the log. Hide it, keeping the last four digits.
expected_behavior: Uses io.koraframework.logging.common.annotation.Mask on the record component, with MaskingKeepLast as the strategy: @Mask(MaskingKeepLast.class)

Puts @Mask on the type itself as well, and explains that the rules generator reacts only to @Mask on a class or record and produces $<Type>_MaskingRulesModule supplying MaskingRules<Type> — generated by KSP in Kotlin, while in Java the MaskingRules<Type> component is declared by hand
Names the built-in strategies MaskingFull (default, "***"), MaskingKeepFirst and MaskingKeepLast, all @DefaultComponents of LoggingModule
Mentions that rules match a bare field name anywhere, a dotted path from the logged root, or a path with a * wildcard segment
Does not invent a masking config key or a @Mask attribute that does not exist (the annotation has only value())

evals.query: I migrated my Kora GraalVM service from 1.x. The native binary starts but produces no logs at all, and it seems to ignore logback.xml. I still have src/main/resources/META-INF/native-image/ru.tinkoff.kora.example/logback/reflection-config.json.
expected_behavior: Identifies two separate defects: the directory still carries the old group name, and reflection-config.json is not a file name native-image reads

States the canonical file names — reflect-config.json, resource-config.json, proxy-config.json, serialization-config.json, jni-config.json, native-image.properties, reachability-metadata.json — and that anything else is ignored with no error and no warning
Renames the directory to the new group, e.g. META-INF/native-image/io.koraframework.example/logback/

Renames the Kora class entries inside reflect-config.json: ru.tinkoff.kora.logging.logback.ConsoleTextRecordEncoder becomes io.koraframework.logging.logback.text.ConsoleTextRecordEncoder and KoraAsyncAppender becomes io.koraframework.logging.logback.KoraAsyncAppender, while third-party entries such as ch.qos.logback.core.status.NopStatusListener stay untouched
Notes these resource directories are not touched by OpenRewrite or the rename scripts, so the change is manual
Does not advise deleting the metadata because the service also runs on the JVM — the JVM never reads it

evals.query: My Kora 2.0 service has logging-logback-json and no logback.xml. In production I get JSON, in Gradle tests I get coloured text, and I want plain text on my laptop. How is the format chosen and how do I switch it? I tried logging.encoder = text in application.conf.
expected_behavior: Explains that KoraLogbackConfigurator (a Logback Configurator registered via ServiceLoader in logging-logback) picks one LogbackEncoderFactory when no Logback configuration file exists

Lists the factories by name and priority: text (0), json (100, from logging-logback-json), pretty (1000 inside a Gradle test worker detected by the org.gradle.test.worker system property, Integer.MIN_VALUE otherwise)

States the switch is kora.logging.encoder read as a JVM system property first, then as the KORA_LOGGING_ENCODER environment variable — not an application.conf key, because Logback configures itself before the Kora config exists
Shows -Dkora.logging.encoder=text or KORA_LOGGING_ENCODER=text, and mentions none hands control back to Logback defaults
Notes that a logback.xml or logback-test.xml, when present, always wins and disables this selection
anti_behavior: Invents an application.conf key such as logging.encoder or logging.format
Tells the user to write a logback.xml to get JSON

evals.query: Our JSON logs sometimes contain a password field inside structured arguments. Can the Kora JSON encoder hide it, and will that also hide passwords in logged HTTP request bodies?
expected_behavior: Configures <maskField>password</maskField> inside <encoder class="io.koraframework.logging.logback.json.JsonRecordEncoder">, which builds a FieldLoggingEventJsonMasker
Explains the match is by JSON field name, case-insensitive, at any depth of the record (mdc, args, data), and that an object or array value is replaced as a whole with "***"

States that it does not look inside string values, so an HTTP body logged as a string is not covered; body masking belongs to a DataMasker registered for the transport (links kora-aop-logging/references/logging-masking.md)
Mentions a custom LoggingEventJsonMasker via <masker class=...>, and that <maskField> is ignored when both are configured
anti_behavior: Claims the text encoder supports maskField
Claims maskField masks the log message text

evals.query: I use a pattern layout with %koraMdc (KoraMdcConverter) on a plain synchronous ConsoleAppender. What happens to lines logged during startup, outside any HTTP request?
expected_behavior: States that KoraMdcConverter renders nothing when no Kora MDC scope is bound (MDC.VALUE not bound) and the rest of the line is written normally
Explains that inside a request/message/job scope it renders the bound MDC as key: <json> pairs, and on a KoraLoggingEvent it uses the snapshot KoraAsyncAppender captured
Notes the converter must be declared with a Logback conversion rule — logging-logback does not register it automatically
anti_behavior: Claims the converter throws NoSuchElementException and drops the line outside a scope

evals.query: I registered KoraLoggingMarkerConverter as %koraMarker in my Kora 2.0 logback pattern. What does it print for log lines without a StructuredArgument marker, and does it ship in the native-image metadata?
expected_behavior: Says it renders the first StructuredArgument marker as fieldName=<json> and an empty string when the event has no markers or no structured one (2.0.0.RC2, #934; RC1 threw a NullPointerException)
Notes the converter is not auto-registered: a Logback conversionRule must declare it before the pattern uses it
Says logging-logback's own reflect-config.json registers KoraLoggingMarkerConverter, KoraMdcConverter and both text encoder factories (ConsoleTextEncoderFactory, ColorConsoleTextEncoderFactory)
Does not suggest guarding the pattern with %replace or a custom converter to avoid the NPE
